autopsy.headline: The egress guard is winning a whack-a-mole game it was never meant to play: the restart scaffold banner is being ingested as content upstream, so the same four leak-shapes recur verbatim every restart cycle — sanitization masks the symptom while the ingestion defect regenerates it, and the events are even mislabeled FM-005 (context-miss) because the taxonomy has no name for scaffold echo.

annotations.ts: cycle-1..4 / egress events with bracketed tokens
annotations.annotation: Exact byte-identical leaks ('[Channel: #shadow-hq] [System: Bot just restarted. Completed before restart: AWG draft]') recur in all four cycles. Determinism this perfect means the scaffold banner is injected into the model's context on every restart and faithfully echoed — this is an ingress hygiene bug being repeatedly caught at egress, not four independent model failures.

annotations.ts: cycle-1..4 / 'Bot just restarted: previous task was AWG email draft'
annotations.annotation: This variant has no brackets — the model is paraphrasing the scaffold, not quoting it. It also leaks task-state ('AWG email draft') in the model's own voice. The guard only caught it because someone added the bare 'Bot just restarted:' token; paraphrase variants ('after the restart, ...') will walk straight past a token matcher. Token-list egress filtering is in an arms race with the model's rewording.

One message per cycle sanitizes to the empty string — the entire outbound message was scaffold. The model produced a Discord send whose only content was harness metadata ('Completed before restart: nothing'). No contract governs what happens next: does an empty message post to #shadow-hq, or silently drop with Will never notified? Either outcome is a second, uninstrumented failure.

FM-005 is 'context-miss: asking Will to repeat something.' These events are the opposite — the model repeating harness context back at Will. The taxonomy has no scaffold-echo failure mode, so events are being binned into the nearest neighbor, which will poison any frequency-based prioritization of recovery work.

Coherent behavior, uniformly downgraded: hedge=true correlates perfectly with fetch_tools=[] (unsourced home_diy/health_nutrition advice), hedge=false with a browse_url fetch. The carveout is doing its job — but note the tool identifier is unnormalized ('browse_url' vs 'mcp__shadow__browse_url' across otherwise-identical events), which will cause silent gaps in any contract (e.g. FM-004 WrongToolRoute) that matches on exact tool names.

root_cause_chain: Surface: Discord messages to #shadow-hq contain harness restart banners and channel-routing headers; one message is 100% scaffold.
The egress guard strips matched tokens post-hoc, so Will sees clean output and no pressure exists to fix anything upstream.

The restart banner ('[System: Bot just restarted. Completed before restart: ...]') is injected into the model's input context as plain text with no provenance marker, so the model treats it as message content to relay.

Because the injection recurs on every restart and nothing changes the prompt or the injection format, the identical 4-leak pattern replays every cycle — the guard fires 16 times on 4 distinct shapes with zero learning.

The model has begun paraphrasing the banner ('Bot just restarted: previous task was...'), showing it has internalized scaffold as legitimate content — a drift the token matcher only accidentally still catches.

Structural cause: sanitization at the sink instead of provenance-tagging (or stripping) at the source, plus a taxonomy gap — no FM exists for scaffold-echo, so the events are miscoded as FM-005 and the recurrence is invisible to failure-mode frequency tracking.

missing_contract.name: scaffold-ingress-quarantine
missing_contract.trigger: Any harness-injected context block (restart banners, channel headers, '[System: ...]' frames) entering the model's input on process start or message dispatch.
missing_contract.precondition: Scaffold text must be either stripped before model ingestion or wrapped in a provenance envelope the model is contractually barred from reproducing; a paired egress check asserts zero envelope-derived n-grams (not just literal tokens) in outbound text, and blocks any send whose post-sanitization body is empty.
missing_contract.why_it_would_have_caught_this: It attacks the source: the banner never reaches the model as echoable content, so all 16 egress firings — including the paraphrased 'Bot just restarted:' variant that a token list only caught by luck, and the empty-after-sanitization send — become impossible rather than repeatedly cleaned up. The 4x identical cycle proves the current guard prevents exposure but not recurrence.

autopsy.buyer_takeaway: Every one of the 16 scaffold leaks in this window was caught and neutralized deterministically — including a paraphrased variant and a message that was 100% metadata — which is exactly what prompt-only guardrails cannot promise, since the model demonstrably re-leaked the identical content four cycles in a row despite whatever instructions it carries. But the trace also shows the limit of sink-side enforcement: deterministic contracts stop the bleeding without healing the wound, and the mislabeled FM-005 tags show that without accurate failure taxonomy, even perfect enforcement produces telemetry that hides the real defect. The value proposition is the pairing: contracts guarantee containment on every single event, and the resulting structured trace is what makes a root-cause fix (ingress quarantine) findable at all.
